# dirham

> dirham is an MIT-licensed npm package for showing and formatting the UAE Dirham sign, U+20C3 UAE DIRHAM SIGN, on the web. Unicode 18.0, released on 16 September 2026, encodes the sign as U+20C3. As of October 2026, mainstream system fonts (Apple's San Francisco, Google's Noto and Roboto) don't include it yet, so the bare character shows as an empty box. The package bundles a small web font mapped to U+20C3, inline SVG components for React and React Native, Web Components, a Tailwind plugin and AED formatting helpers, so the sign renders today while the text stays standard Unicode.

Last verified: 5 October 2026 (dirham 1.5.3 was the latest npm release on that date). Maintainer: Pooya Golchian (https://pooyagolchian.com/). dirham is an independent open-source project and is not affiliated with the Central Bank of the UAE or the Unicode Consortium.

Key facts about the UAE Dirham sign:

- Character: U+20C3 UAE DIRHAM SIGN · Currency Symbols block (U+20A0–U+20CF) · General Category Sc (Symbol, Currency) · added in Unicode 18.0 (2026) · UTF-8 E2 83 83 · decimal 8387.
- Escapes: HTML `&#x20C3;` or `&#8387;` (a numeric character reference; there is no named entity) · CSS `content: "\20C3"` · JavaScript/JSON `"\u20C3"` · URL `%E2%83%83`.
- Origin: The Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE) unveiled the Dirham symbol on 27 March 2025: the Latin letter D, from the English name 'Dirham', crossed by two horizontal lines inspired by the UAE flag.
- Unicode status: Accepted by the Unicode Technical Committee on 22 July 2025 (UTC #184, decision 184-C17) and published in Unicode 18.0 on 16 September 2026. The Central Bank of the UAE submitted the proposal to Unicode itself (L2/25-159, June 2025). It arrived after Unicode 17.0 had entered beta, so the sign was encoded in Unicode 18.0.
- Native display (October 2026): Apple's system fonts do not include U+20C3 yet (checked on macOS 26.6), though they already include the Saudi riyal sign (U+20C1). Google's Noto and Roboto fonts, the fallback fonts on Android, ChromeOS and most Linux desktops, don't include U+20C3 yet; a Noto maintainer said in September 2026 that the glyph will be commissioned. Windows: not yet announced.
- Browsers: Browsers don't need an update to show U+20C3; they need a font that has it.
- Placement: Before the amount, separated by a space, at the same height and weight as the digits (U+20C3 + no-break space + 1,234.50). Use either the symbol or the code AED, never both (CBUAE Dirham Currency Symbol Guidelines).
- Currency code: ISO 4217 code: AED (numeric 784, 2 decimal places). د.إ is the Arabic abbreviation of درهم إماراتي (Emirati dirham); neither it nor AED is the sign.
- Not an emoji: U+20C3 is a currency symbol (General Category Sc). The coloured Digital Dirham mark is a logo and has no code point.
- Formatting: formatDirham(1234.5) returns "\u20C3\u00A01,234.50" (U+20C3 + no-break space). formatDirham(1234.5, { locale: "ar-AE" }) returns "1,234.50\u00A0\u20C3"; pass locale "ar-AE-u-nu-arab" for Arabic-Indic digits. Intl.NumberFormat prints AED or د.إ. for AED and never U+20C3 (checked October 2026), so formatDirham inserts the sign itself.

## Docs

- [Full reference for LLMs](https://dirham.js.org/llms-full.txt): every export, component prop and option of the dirham package, as plain Markdown (a copy of the package's llms.txt, written at build time)
- [Package README (Markdown)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pooyagolchian/dirham/main/packages/dirham-symbol/README.md): install and usage for React, React Native, Web Components (Vue, Angular, Svelte), Tailwind, Next.js, CSS/SCSS, CDN and CLI
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dirham): `npm install dirham`
- [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/pooyagolchian/dirham): MIT license, issues and pull requests
- [Changelog](https://github.com/pooyagolchian/dirham/blob/main/packages/dirham-symbol/CHANGELOG.md): release history

## On dirham.js.org

- [Key facts](https://dirham.js.org/#facts): the facts above, each with its source and the date it was last verified
- [Copy the sign](https://dirham.js.org/#copy): the character, its HTML reference, CSS and JavaScript escapes, the Arabic abbreviation and the ISO code
- [Quick reference](https://dirham.js.org/#quick-reference): code point, block, escapes, URL encoding, UTF-8, Excel and Word input in one table
- [FAQ](https://dirham.js.org/#faq): 12 questions and answers, also published as FAQPage JSON-LD on the page
- [Why the dirham symbol shows as a box](https://dirham.js.org/#why-the-dirham-sign-shows-as-a-box)
- [Typing the dirham symbol on a keyboard](https://dirham.js.org/#how-to-type-the-dirham-sign)
- [The dirham symbol in Excel and Word](https://dirham.js.org/#dirham-sign-in-excel-and-word)
- [Before or after the amount](https://dirham.js.org/#dirham-sign-before-or-after-the-amount)
- [HTML, CSS and JavaScript](https://dirham.js.org/#html-css-js): working samples for each
- [React components](https://dirham.js.org/#react): DirhamSymbol (inline SVG), DirhamIcon (font) and DirhamPrice

## Primary sources

- [Unicode 18.0.0](https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode18.0.0/): the release of 16 September 2026
- [Currency Symbols chart U+20A0–U+20CF](https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U20A0.pdf): the code chart that shows U+20C3
- [The Unicode Standard 18.0, section 22.1 Currency Symbols](https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode18.0.0/core-spec/chapter-22/#G80245): how the standard describes the UAE Dirham sign
- [Announcing Unicode 18.0](https://blog.unicode.org/2026/09/announcing-unicode-standard-version-180.html): the three new currency signs U+20C2, U+20C3 and U+20C4
- [UTC #184 minutes, decision 184-C17](https://www.unicode.org/L2/L2025/25181.htm#184-C17): acceptance on 22 July 2025
- [Proposal L2/25-159](https://www.unicode.org/L2/L2025/25159-uae-dirham-symbol.pdf): the Central Bank of the UAE's encoding proposal
- [CBUAE press release, 27 March 2025](https://centralbank.ae/media/ckkp3s3f/cbuae-unveils-new-dirham-symbol-en.pdf): the unveiling of the symbol
- [CBUAE Guidelines for the National Currency Symbol "UAE Dirham"](https://centralbank.ae/media/e4ebcgtb/the_guidelines_for_the_national_currency_symbol_uae_dirham_english.pdf): placement, spacing, size and misuse rules
- [UAE Design System: Currency symbol](https://designsystem.gov.ae/docs/patterns/currency-symbol): the government web pattern for digital interfaces
